title: Linear independence of product functions
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $I$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, and let $B=(b_a)_{a\in I}$ be a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$, with one basis function constantly equal to $1$. For every natural number $n$, the functions on $\Omega^n$ given by $x\mapsto\prod_{j=1}^n b_{a_j}(x_j)$, indexed by tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in I^n$, are linearly independent over $\mathbb R$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty index set $I$ with decidable equality
A real basis of functions on $\Omega$
The distinguished basis vector is constantly $1$
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
